prediction.beta: New mode in testing — predict BTC's 5-minute direction. Prices, settlement rule and taker fees follow polymarket.com.
prediction.title: BTC 5-minute prediction
prediction.targetTip: Chainlink 60-second time-weighted average price (TWAP) at the moment the round opened; this is Polymarket's price to beat. Settlement uses the 60-second TWAP at the close: at or above it is Up, below is Down.
prediction.upTip: Probability price: 50¢ = the market gives a 50% chance of going up. Higher price, stronger conviction.
prediction.downTip: Probability price: 50¢ = the market gives a 50% chance of going down. Higher price, stronger conviction.
prediction.estPayoutTip: Right prediction: every contract settles at $1. Payout = amount ÷ probability price; the fee is charged on top of the amount.
prediction.feeTip: Polymarket taker fee: shares × 7% × price × (1 − price). Most expensive at 50¢ (1.75¢ per share), cheaper toward the extremes.
prediction.estProceedsTip: What you receive at the current sell price, after fees.
prediction.mySharesTip: Contracts you hold; each is worth $1 if the prediction is right.

jev.title: Jev predictor
jev.intro: Jev bets on BTC's 5-minute up/down market like a player: every 15 seconds after the open it looks at the market and gives the chance that UP wins this window. Code sets that chance against both asks, buys only when a side is still worth it after the fee, and stakes more the bigger the edge; code decides by fair value when to sell a position or hold it to settlement.
jev.archivedBanner: Viewing archived run {{n}}: it no longer bets, and its bets, decisions and scores stay as they ended.
jev.pnlLabel: PnL this run · settled bets, after fees
jev.scoreDetailsSub: How accurate is Jev's win chance? · {{n}} samples
jev.brierExplain: At every checkpoint the three chances of UP are checked against the result: UP counts as 1, DOWN as 0, and we average (chance − result)². 0 is perfect; 0.25 is what always guessing 50% gets.
jev.brierHow: Watch Jev: lower than Market means Jev reads the window better than the market, which betting on its win chance needs to make money; lower than Math means it beats the formula that only looks at the gap and the time left. The lowest in each row is orange.
jev.calibration: Calibration: does 70% come true 70% of the time?
jev.calibrationExplain: Jev's chances are split into five bands, and each band shows how often BTC actually finished UP. In the 60%–80% band, roughly seven in ten should have gone UP. The bar is the actual share, the tick is the band's average forecast; the closer the bar's end is to the tick, the better.
jev.guideAction: The first line is what actually happened this time (Buy UP / Buy DOWN / Sell / Hold / Stay out), how much was staked, the time, and how many seconds after the open.
jev.guideEdge: "Jev's edge per share UP +7¢": Jev's win chance set against both asks — how much more each share on the better side should earn (win chance − ask − fee). It buys at {{minEdge}}¢ or more; rows while holding don't have this line.
jev.guideUpChance: The three "Chance of UP" numbers estimate the same thing — will this window finish above the target price — in different ways:
jev.guideModel: From how far BTC is above the target, how many seconds are left, and how much BTC has been moving lately. While holding, code uses it as the fair price to decide when to sell.
jev.guideJev: Jev's own win chance: one request asks both "will this settle UP?" and "will this settle DOWN?", and the number is the average of UP-wins and 1 − DOWN-wins. When flat, code uses it to decide whether to buy and which side.
jev.guideMkt: Derived from the UP and DOWN prices in the order book. With UP around 67¢ and DOWN around 35¢, the market thinks about 66% UP.
jev.guideCompare: When Jev is above Market, Jev thinks UP is cheap; the other way round, DOWN. It only buys when the gap is still {{minEdge}}¢ or more after the fee.
jev.guideFold: Routine stay-out / hold rows are folded; use "Show all" on the right of each window. Click any row to see Jev's answer to both questions.
jev.guideLegacy: R1 is the old version: Jev picked the trade itself and judged whether the move still had legs, and its Jev column is the momentum-adjusted math chance. R1 rows are shown as they were.
jev.guideQuestionsTitle: What Jev is asked each time
jev.qWinsDesc: Asked at every checkpoint, flat or holding. The same request asks it both ways: will the final-minute average end at or above the opening average (UP wins), and will it end below (DOWN wins). Jev answers with probabilities; averaging the two framings cancels out any lean from the wording.
jev.guideBuy: When flat, each side's edge per share = Jev's win chance for that side − ask − fee, and code takes the larger: one stake at {{minEdge}}¢ or more, two at {{bigEdge}}¢ or more, and no buy when the ask is below {{minAsk}}¢. When the wallet cannot afford a bet it stops itself until a new run.
jev.guideSell: While holding, Jev is not consulted: code sells when the bid, net of fee, is {{sellEdge}}¢ or more above the math fair price, otherwise holds to settlement. After selling it can buy again in the same window.
jev.q1Title: Does the move still have legs?
